notes:
T849 (scratch-repo fixture: helper + batch 1). Advances L1. Builds the ONE place a scratch git repo is created and converts a first batch of FIVE single-`git init` scripts through it. No claim status is changed and none is proposed; this is a mechanism + tooling record.

CENSUS — VERIFIED, matches the seat's: 83 regression scripts in tools/; 58 contain `git init`; 77 `git init` calls in total (51 scripts with exactly 1, 4 with 2, 1 with 4, 2 with 7). Scratch roots: 65 use `/tmp/weizigo/...`, 11 use `/private/tmp/weizigo/...` (same dir via the /tmp -> /private/tmp symlink on this host); 3 use the `name.XXXXXX` dot variant (complementarity, pilot-gate-seed, pilot-gate-fakebin). Commands: `grep -l 'git init' tools/regression-*.sh | wc -l` = 58; `grep -rl 'git init' tools/regression-*.sh | while read f; do grep -c 'git init' "$f"; done | sort | uniq -c` = 51/1, 4/2, 1/4, 2/7.

DELIVERABLE 1 — tools/lib/scratch-repo.sh: sourceable helper, the only place a scratch repo is made. Unsets GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY GIT_NAMESPACE before any git command (at source time AND inside the function, so a re-set env between calls cannot sneak through). Normalises the scratch root to its real path (resolves /tmp -> /private/tmp once at source time, then `pwd -P` on each mktemp dir) so a child git never traverses the symlink. `git init -q <path>`. Refuses on mktemp/git-init failure (returns 2; under `set -e` that aborts the script — T445 preserved). `weizigo_scratch_repo <slug> [outvar]` sets a caller-named variable (default WEIZIGO_SCRATCH_DIR) via `printf -v`, so the 7-call scripts can hold several repos at once. No options beyond slug/outvar.

DELIVERABLE 2 — tools/regression-scratch-repo.sh: 4 ARMS. A null (healthy call -> working repo, REAL repo untouched: worktree unset, tree count unchanged, toplevel ok). B seeded-defect (the incident, RED then GREEN): the OLD hand-rolled pattern, run with GIT_DIR aimed at a THROWAWAY victim repo, truncated the victim 5 files -> 1 and set its core.worktree (incident reproduced — RED, control has teeth); the helper, with the SAME inherited GIT_DIR, left a fresh throwaway victim intact (tree 5 -> 5, worktree still unset) and built its own working repo (GREEN). The old-pattern arm is NEVER run against this repository. C idempotence (two calls -> two distinct working repos). D cleanup (three dirs created under the normalised root, `rm -rf` clears all three, no accumulation). Red-then-green is genuine for arm B; arms A/C/D are invariant assertions (per the standing tooling rule, permitted when a defect cannot be re-observed failing in the thing under test) and each names the invariant it would catch. Result: ALL 4 ARMS PASSED.

DELIVERABLE 3 — tools/scratch-repo-equivalence.sh: for a named tracked script, runs HEAD's version (before) and the working-tree version (after) from the script's REAL path (so $0/`dirname`/PROJECT resolve identically — scripts derive PROJECT from $0), captures stdout+stderr+exit, normalises scratch paths (`/tmp/weizigo/<slug>-XXXXXX` and `/private/tmp/...` and git's `Initialized empty Git repository in <path>/.git/` line all reduce to <SCRATCH>), and asserts byte-identical normalised output AND equal exit code. The before-version is read with `git show HEAD:` and installed at the real path for the run, then the working-tree version is restored (trap-guarded, so an interrupted run never leaves the before-version in the tree). THE HARNESS PROVED RELIABLE: it caught a real behaviour change — regression-managent-status-json uses `git init "$TMPDIR"` WITHOUT -q, so it emits `Initialized empty Git repository in <path>/.git/` to stdout; the helper's `git init -q` suppresses that line, and the harness correctly flagged the would-be mismatch, which is why status-json was NOT converted (see resistance list). It also trivially reports EQUIVALENT on unchanged scripts (self-check: ran it on all 5 targets pre-edit -> EQUIVALENT).

FIVE CONVERSIONS (one commit each, bisectable): regression-managent-standing (ac... no — c146b2b), regression-managent-store-write-utf8 (10742bb), regression-managent-resume (cb87336), regression-managent-done-git (b433997), regression-orient (09a0c46). Each: syntax-checked (`bash -n`), run through the equivalence harness (all EQUIVALENT, exit 0 == exit 0), run directly (all exit 0, ALL CONTROLS PASSED), then committed. Post-commit invariants checked after every commit: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` = this repo, `git config --get core.worktree` unset, `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD | wc -l` = 2647 (>2000), `git show HEAD:.gitignore | wc -l` = 46 — all green throughout. Picked these five because each is self-equivalent (deterministic under scratch-path normalisation), has exactly one `git init` line invoked once, has the mktemp dir BE the repo (Pattern A: `cd $WORK; git init -q`, or Pattern B: `git init -q $TMPDIR`), and uses `git init -q` (quiet, so no `Initialized...` banner is emitted to preserve). Spread: 4 Pattern A + 1 Pattern B.

HOW LONG ONE CONVERSION TAKES (machine-measured on this host, conversion 3 / resume): equivalence-harness run 0.48s real; the converted script run 0.20s real; the commit is dominated by the pre-commit fast tier (~30s wall, budget 45s). The edit itself is a few minutes of agent time for the mechanical single-init case (source the lib, replace the mktemp+`git init` block, keep trap/cd). So the per-conversion wall is roughly: agent-edit (a few min) + 0.7s verification + ~30s pre-commit; the verification is cheap, the commit gate is the floor.

SCRIPTS EXPECTED TO RESIST MECHANICAL CONVERSION (named, for the seat to scope the later batches):
- regression-managent-holds.sh (1 git init, but mktemp dir is a PARENT; the repo is a subdirectory $ROOT/repo with a sibling $ROOT/scratch store — the helper makes the mktemp dir BE the repo, so a direct swap changes structure).
- regression-managent-status-json.sh (1 git init, but `git init "$TMPDIR"` WITHOUT -q — emits `Initialized empty Git repository in <path>/.git/` to stdout, which the helper's -q would suppress; equivalence harness flags it. Fix by adding -q in the same conversion, which is a one-token change but is a behaviour edit the harness correctly catches — convert with the -q added and re-run equivalence).
- regression-managent-impression-gate.sh (1 `git init` LINE, but it lives inside a setup() function called 6x on subdirs $WORK/S1..N3 — the mktemp dir is a parent of 6 repos, not the repo; not the mechanical single-init case).
- The multi-init scripts (4 with 2, 1 with 4, 2 with 7 — regression-managent-integrity, regression-model-profiles, regression-process-ownership, regression-race-collect, regression-absorption-machinery, regression-git-commit-mine-hook, regression-precommit) — explicitly deferred to the seat's sign-off per the brief.
- Scripts that are NOT self-equivalent under scratch-path normalisation (regression-task-identity, regression-arbiter, regression-argus-doctor, regression-claim-lifecycle, regression-directive-kill, regression-fleet-keeper, regression-inbox-loop, regression-runner-guard, regression-runner-harness-p95, regression-runner-reap, regression-runner-reporting, regression-watch-fleet, regression-window-resilience) — the equivalence harness cannot validate a conversion of these until their pre-existing nondeterminism (pids/timestamps/state) is normalised or the script is made deterministic; converting them blind would assert nothing.

GAPS / FOLLOW-UPS FOR THE SEAT:
1. The new controls are NOT wired into `zig build test` nor the pre-commit fast-tier pool. Wiring needs an edit to build.zig (and/or tools/hooks/pre-commit's FAST_POOL), both OUTSIDE this task's declared deliverables — the staged-path backstop (and tools/git-commit-mine) refuse them under the T849 identity. Recommendation: a follow-up task with build.zig + tools/hooks/pre-commit in its scope wires `tools/regression-scratch-repo.sh` into the fast tier (it is ~0.2s, host-insensitive, deterministic) so the helper's controls run on every commit, per the standing tooling rule 'a tooling task is not accepted until its test is wired into zig build test'. Until then the controls are runnable by hand (`bash tools/regression-scratch-repo.sh`) and pass.
2. The five conversion commits were made with `tools/git-commit-mine --explicit` because the converted scripts are not in the bundle's deliverables= list (only the 4 mechanism files are). The brief explicitly instructs converting and committing the five, so --explicit (the documented 'wrapper took responsibility' channel) was the honest route; recorded here so the seat sees the scope mismatch and can either ratify the conversions or add 'converted scripts' to future batches' deliverables.
3. 53 single-init scripts remain; the seat sets the batch size for the rest from this report. The mechanical cost per script is low (a few min + 0.7s verify + ~30s commit); the binding constraint is the resistance list above.
